messages.subject: Re: Issues with duplicate entries
messages.body_plain:
If anyone is still having problems with this I solved it.  The problem of having modified an unmodified peptides can be fixed by making a new report type by editing the MSstatsInput report under view->document grid.  Go to customize view, rename the new view to something else, and add the "Modified Peptide sequence" to the report in place of "PeptideSequence", then remove the "peptideSequence" column, and rename the "Modified Peptide Sequence" to "PeptideSequence".  Then MSstats can see that modified and unmodified versions of the peptide are in fact different (which was concealed by using "Peptide sequence" instead of modified peptide sequence).  You then need to go to Tools-> external tools and change the input report to the report you just made

Further, if you want to trick it to think each form of a peptide is a protein for PTM-centered analysis, replace the proteinName column with "peptideSequence" or "Modified Peptide Sequence" and rename that column to "proteinName".

Hope that helps.

Best,
Jesse

messages.subject: Re: Parallelization of dataProcess
messages.body_plain:
I would like to propose a suggestion to the developers of MSstats. Would it be possible to introduce a parameter parallelCalculation = TRUE|FALSE (default FALSE) for dataProcess that is passed to .runQuantification and evaluated in the sense that the 1:nlevel(data$PROTEIN) loops use a foreach construct instead of a for to loop if set to TRUE ?

I guess this could be done comparatively easy without having to change the algorithm itself very much. This way speed performance could be improved dramatically.

kind regards,
Thomas

messages.subject: Re: SUBJECT_NESTED
messages.body_plain:
Dear Users,

First of all, Thank you Petri for addressing this issue.

We found that this issue came from csv file. If you save the output('ProcessedData') of 'dataProcess' function as csv file, 4.1 and 4.10 become as the same 4.10 (numeric value) in the example above. However, 'Run' column still distinguish 4.1 and 4.10 as different number. If you didn't save it as csv file and re-read it, which means just use 'dataProcess' and use 'groupComparion' with the output of 'dataProcess', there is no problem at all. You can check the correct SUBJECT_NESTED and RUN column information with the command lines below,

quant<-dataProcess(raw)
quantprocess<-quant$ProcessedData
unique(quantprocess[,c("SUBJECT","SUBJECT_NESTED","RUN")]

However, we will change the way to assign SUBJECT_NESTED column in order to prevent this confusion.
Thank you.

-Meena

messages.body_plain:

Thanks for your suggestion. We'll definitely be looking into that. We are planning to put efforts on improving modularization of MSstats, and the implementation for parallel computation will probably happen thereafter.

P.S. If you use spike-in standard to normalize the data, one way to get around at this point is to split your dataset into subsets and assign them to available cores accordingly.

Best,
Tsung-Heng

messages.subject: Re: Parallelization of dataProcess
messages.body_plain:
Hi Thomas,

Also, as a short-term workaround, I suggest to reduce the number of features per protein. I really doubt that you need all the 156 peptides per protein to perform protein-level relative quantification. Selecting some number of features with highest average/median intensity across all the replicates will go a long way to speed up the process. In our experience, this will not undermine the performance.

I hope this helps
Olga
